Build a reusable personal prompt chain to iterate brand copy (belongs in ai-tool-direction)
Compare an AI production step with the current process using a test set and scoring rule (belongs in ai-tool-evaluation)

cards.name: Team coordination, performance management, and people management (incl. HR)
cards.includes: This bundle covers coordinating print, packaging, or creative production teams with a clear understanding of roles and responsibilities, especially when project pressure threatens communication. It includes addressing performance gaps in real time and understanding the basics of hiring, onboarding, and performance/HR policy. It also covers carrying out a hire, an onboarding plan, or a documented performance review end-to-end for a real or simulated team, recognizing that people-management decisions have consequences beyond one project.
cards.excludes: Planning and controlling the full project life cycle belongs in project-management; managing client sign-offs and expectations belongs in project-oversight. Selecting, briefing, and reviewing outside production vendors belongs in vendor-management. Being a good member of a team on shared work belongs in collaboration, and leading an organization's AI adoption belongs in ai-strategy-change-leadership.
cards.distinctions: Unlike project-management, which owns scope, schedules, budgets, and project control, team-coordination focuses on production-team roles, communication under pressure, and individual performance. Unlike project-oversight, it centers internal team coordination and people management rather than client approvals and expectations. Unlike vendor-management, it addresses team members and hiring, onboarding, or performance review rather than selecting and managing outside suppliers.
positiveExamples: Coordinate production-team roles and preserve communication during a high-pressure print job.
Address a team member's performance gap in real time during a packaging project.
Carry out and document a performance review end-to-end for a real or simulated production-team member.
negativeExamples: Build and re-baseline a packaging project's schedule as scope and delivery dates change (belongs in project-management)
Manage client approvals and explain delivery trade-offs during a print project (belongs in project-oversight)
Select and review a finishing vendor for a complex production job (belongs in vendor-management)

cards.name: Vendor selection, management, and relationship maintenance
cards.includes: This bundle covers understanding the capabilities and limitations of major print and packaging vendor categories and selecting a vendor suited to a complex project's requirements. It includes briefing the vendor on specifications, managing its work through delivery, and conducting a post-project review. It also covers maintaining vendor relationships as long-term investments, including understanding how trust affects what vendors can and will do under pressure.
cards.excludes: Overall project planning and change control belong in project-management, while cost estimation and budget management belong in cost-management. Conducting price or terms negotiations belongs in negotiation-persuasion, and resolving contract or licensing risks belongs in contracts-ip-licensing. Managing the client's service relationship belongs in customer-relationship-management.
cards.distinctions: Unlike project-management, which runs the overall project plan across teams and vendors, this bundle focuses on selecting and managing the external vendor. Unlike cost-management, it centers on vendor capability, delivery, and relationship continuity rather than estimating costs and controlling spend. Unlike negotiation-persuasion, it covers the ongoing vendor relationship rather than a negotiation over price, scope, or terms.
positiveExamples: Compare print and packaging vendors' capabilities and limitations to select one for a complex job.
Brief a selected vendor on job specifications and manage its work through delivery.
Review vendor performance after a project and use the findings to maintain the relationship and set realistic expectations for future rush work.
negativeExamples: Build and update the overall schedule, dependencies, and change-control record for a packaging project (belongs in project-management)
Prepare a production cost estimate and track spending through delivery (belongs in cost-management)
Negotiate a vendor's price and payment terms against a defined walk-away point (belongs in negotiation-persuasion)

cards.name: Workflow platform configuration and operation
cards.includes: This bundle covers designing or configuring workflows for creative, print, packaging, and brand production work, on a platform such as Workfront or Monday or on paper. It includes structuring intake, proofing, approvals, and reporting, and sequencing human and AI work so handoffs maintain quality and efficiency. The focus is on workflow patterns, configuration, and sequencing rather than the choice of any single tool.
cards.excludes: Building scripts, API integrations, or low-code automations that transfer work between systems belongs in systems-automation-integration. Re-engineering print or packaging production processes belongs in workflow-design, while building or operating the substantive quality and compliance review checks belongs in quality-frameworks.
cards.distinctions: Unlike workflow-design, which designs or re-engineers the production process itself, workflow-architecture structures intake, proofing, approvals, reporting, and handoffs in a workflow platform or paper design. Unlike systems-automation-integration, it sequences work rather than building connections between systems. Unlike project-management, it defines how work moves through the workflow rather than managing a project's scope, schedule, budget, and delivery.
positiveExamples: Configure a workflow platform's intake, proofing, approval, and reporting steps for a print campaign.
Map a packaging creative workflow on paper, sequencing AI-assisted work and human approvals at handoff points.
Revise workflow sequencing to prevent artwork from reaching production before required approval.
negativeExamples: Build an API integration that sends artwork between a creative system and an AI review system (belongs in systems-automation-integration)
Re-engineer a packaging production step and validate its effect on throughput and quality (belongs in workflow-design)
Build and operate a review checklist that catches regulatory errors in AI-assisted artwork (belongs in quality-frameworks)

cards.name: Production workflow design, process engineering, and optimization
cards.includes: This bundle covers designing production workflows for multi-component print and packaging projects using standard offset, digital, flexo, and packaging workflow patterns. It also covers re-sequencing, automating, or re-tooling an existing production process to change its throughput, quality, or cost. Work here balances quality, timeline, and budget constraints with trade-offs among throughput, quality, and adaptability, and validates process changes before they replace a working process.
cards.excludes: Running project schedules, tracking changes, and reporting status belong in project-management; configuring intake, approval, proofing, and reporting workflows belongs in workflow-architecture. Building scripts, API integrations, or low-code connections between systems belongs in systems-automation-integration, rather than here.
cards.distinctions: Unlike project-management, which plans and runs a project through delivery, workflow-design determines how production steps are arranged to meet the project's constraints or improve the production process itself. Unlike workflow-architecture, which sequences intake, approvals, proofing, and reporting, this bundle focuses on the production process and its throughput, quality, cost, and adaptability. Unlike systems-automation-integration, it addresses whether and how automation changes production performance, rather than building the connection between systems.
positiveExamples: Design a production sequence for a multi-component print and packaging project that meets quality, deadline, and budget constraints.
Re-sequence a production step to improve throughput and validate its quality and cost effects before replacing the existing process.
Compare production workflow alternatives for their trade-offs in throughput, quality, and adaptability.
negativeExamples: Track schedule slippage and report project status across production teams (belongs in project-management)
Configure a platform's intake forms, proof approvals, and reporting steps (belongs in workflow-architecture)
Build an API integration that transfers job data between two systems (belongs in systems-automation-integration)

cards.name: Written communication
cards.includes: This bundle covers writing clear, organized documents suited to their reader: briefs, reports, specifications and messages that the reader can act on without follow-up. It is shown through graded writing whose rubric assesses the writing itself, not only the content.
cards.excludes: Speaking, presenting and listening belong in spoken-communication. A proposal's business case and ROI argument belong in proposal-development, and client reports interpreting results belong in results-interpretation. Visual communication belongs in the technical bundles.
cards.distinctions: Unlike spoken-communication, it is communication in writing. Unlike proposal-development and results-interpretation, which are business skills that use writing, this bundle is the general ability to write clearly for a reader.
positiveExamples: Write a production specification a printer can quote from without follow-up questions.
Write a project report organized so a manager can find the decision needed.
Write a client email that explains a change and what is needed from them.
negativeExamples: Present a project to a client and answer their questions (belongs in spoken-communication)
Build the ROI case in a proposal to win a client (belongs in proposal-development)
Design a layout that communicates a brand message visually (belongs in the technical bundles)
